Description: The Department handcuffs Bioenginering as hub for research and teaching at the interface of biology, engineering and physical sciences. In synergistic parallel, the application of novel technologies and concepts emerging from these same engineering disciplines is rapidly advancing the science of biology. Taken together these two endeavors –engineering from biology and engineering for biology– comprise the discipline of bioengineering, a field that combines discoveries in the life sciences with the fundamental principles of engineering in furtherance of both. The Biological Engineering PhD will train students in fundamental discovery, experimental methods, quantitative analysis, and technological design, innovation and application and prepare them for careers in all areas of biological engineering.

Concentration: ['Financial Mathematics & Statistics', 'Quantitative Methods in Social Sciences']
Description: The Department of Statistics and Applied Probability (PSTAT) is a diverse community engaged in education and research. Our 21 faculty members are actively involved in interdisciplinary research spanning Financial Mathematics, Data Science, Actuarial Science, Theoretical Statistics, Applied Probability, Applied Statistics, and Biostatistics. We actively recruit the highest-quality faculty and graduate students. The PhD program prepares students to expand the boundaries of statistical theory and practice. With rigorous training in mathematical statistics, probability, and applied methods, students develop research skills that allow them to produce scholarship in exciting areas of data science, statistics, applied probability, and mathematical finance. [18, 20] We are also home to more than 100 graduate students in programs including BS/MS in Actuarial Science, MA in Applied Statistics and PhD in Statistics and Applied Probability, including emphases in Financial Mathematics & Statistics, and Quantitative Methods in Social Sciences. [20]

ProgramName: Master of Technology Management
Doctor of Philosophy in Technology Management
Description: TTechnology Manage­ment’s doc­toral pro­gram is designed to pro­duce excep­tional schol­ars who study technology-related work, tech­no­log­i­cal change, and inno­va­tion who will go on to research and teach at top uni­ver­si­ties across the coun­try and around the world. The cur­ricu­lum inte­grates orga­ni­za­tional stud­ies with tech­nol­ogy and inno­va­tion stud­ies in an inter­dis­ci­pli­nary envi­ron­ment that tran­scends the dis­tinc­tions between dis­ci­plines. We wel­come appli­ca­tions from indi­vid­u­als with back­grounds in the social sci­ences, phys­i­cal sci­ences, man­age­ment, or engi­neer­ing. If you come from a tech­nol­ogy or sci­en­tific back­ground, we will teach you about the impor­tance of orga­ni­za­tions and social sys­tems. If you have a social sci­ence or man­age­ment back­ground, you will learn to under­stand the role of tech­nol­ogy and inno­va­tion in shap­ing orga­ni­za­tional action.

ProgramName: Master of Arts in Theater, Dance, and Performance Studies
Master of Arts/Doctor of Philosophy in Theater, Dance, and Performance Studies
Description: The Department of Theater and Dance relates academic study of theater, dance, and performance studies to a rich field of interdisciplinary studies. The M.A. program affords a strong foundation for work in educational or professional theater, dance, and performance, or for further graduate study. The Ph.D. is an intensive program concentrating in literary, critical, and historical research, designed to prepare students for university teaching.

ProgramName: Doctor of Philosophy in Theater, Dance, and Performance Studies
Emphasis in Ancient Mediterranean Studies
Description: The Emphasis in Ancient Mediterranean Studies (AMS) is an interdisciplinary program at the University of California, Santa Barbara, that provides graduate students with the opportunity to cross the conventional disciplinary lines in the study of the Mediterranean regions from the Bronze Age to the Early Middle Ages. [12, 14] The program includes faculty from the departments of Anthropology, Classics, History, History of Art and Architecture, and Religious Studies. [12] Students pursuing a Ph.D. in these participating departments can petition to add this emphasis. [14] The program gives students access to a wide array of course offerings and faculty across these departments. [12]

ProgramName: Emphasis in Applied Linguistics
Department: An interdisciplinary emphasis offered by the Graduate Division in collaboration with the following Ph.D. programs: Comparative Literature, East Asian Languages and Cultural Studies, Education, Hispanic Languages & Literatures, and Linguistics. [2]
Concentration: Optional Ph.D. Emphasis in Applied Linguistics
Description: The field of applied linguistics is a growing and vibrant one in universities nationally and internationally. Applied linguistics is an interdisciplinary field of research and instruction that provides theoretical and descriptive foundations for the empirical investigation<ctrl100> of language-related issues, especially those of language education (first-language, second-language, foreign-language, and heritage-language teaching and learning), but also issues of bilingualism and biliteracy, language planning and policy, language assessment, translation and interpretation, lexicography, rhetoric, and composition. [9] Students pursuing a Ph.D. in the Departments of Education, French and Italian, Germanic, Slavic, and Semitic Studies, Linguistics, and Spanish and Portuguese may petition to add an emphasis in applied linguistics. [9]
ScholarshipType: Merit-based fellowships, research assistantships, teaching assistantships, and the Dorothy Chun and Joseph Polchinski Studies in Applied Linguistics Fellowship. [2, 14, 16]

ProgramName: Emphasis in Asian American Studies
Description: Asian American Studies is fundamentally interdisciplinary in nature, intersectional in practice and transnational in perspective, and the Asian American Studies Emphasis (AASE) represents an important development in the critical, interdisciplinary graduate education offered at UCSB. [36] This Emphasis offers a graduate level study of the history and subjectivities of Asian Americans by world-renowned scholars who teach, research, and serve Asian American communities. [36] Students pursuing the emphasis in Asian American Studies will successfully complete four graduate courses that have been approved by the Doctoral Emphasis advisor. [36] An AASE-participating faculty member will serve on the candidate's dissertation committee. [36] Applicants must first be admitted to, or currently enrolled in, a UCSB Ph.D. program participating in the Asian American Studies graduate emphasis: English, Feminist Studies, Global Studies, History, Religious Studies, and Sociology. [36]
ScholarshipType: Fellowships, Teaching Assistantships, Research Assistantships, Grants

ProgramName: Emphasis in Black Studies
Fees: The university provides a general cost of attendance for graduate students, as a specific fee for the 'Emphasis in Black Studies' is not available. The total estimated cost for a graduate student living on campus for the 2025-2026 academic year is not explicitly provided on the graddiv.ucsb.edu website, but pages on cost of attendance exist. [114, 117]
Concentration: Interdisciplinary Ph.D. Emphasis in Black Studies
Description: An optional graduate emphasis that is a focused area of study offered as an addition to an existing graduate degree program. [25] The Department of Black Studies at the University of California, Santa Barbara has launched the Black Studies Emphasis (BSE) for students enrolled in doctoral programs in various departments. [28] The BSE builds on the university's strengths in Race Studies, Comparative Ethnicity, and the Black experience, positioning UCSB as a leader in Black Studies and Social Justice research and pedagogy. [28] Students are required to complete five courses designed to develop a critical and analytical understanding of racial theory and pedagogy, as well as the study of Black people in local and global contexts. [28] In addition to coursework, candidates must have a Black Studies faculty member on their dissertation committee. [28] The emphasis focuses on five broad areas of inquiry: Race Studies, The Black Studies traditions of criticality, activism, social justice, sustainability, and transgressive epistemology, Sexual and Gender Studies, African Culture and Identity in America and throughout the Diaspora, and Comparative Ethnic Studies Likely. [28]
ScholarshipType: Funding for doctoral students is typically managed by the student's home department and may include a combination of fellowships, teaching assistantships, and research assistantships. [105, 113, 116]

ProgramName: Emphasis in Cognitive Science
Department: The Emphasis in Cognitive Science is an interdisciplinary program and not housed in a single school. Participating departments come from the College of Letters and Science, the Gevirtz Graduate School of Education, and the College of Engineering. [98]
Description: The University of California, Santa Barbara offers a PhD Emphasis in Cognitive Science. Doctoral students from twelve affiliated departments (Anthropology, Communication, Comparative Literature, Computer Science, Education, English, Geography, Linguistics, Media Arts & Technology, Music, Philosophy, and Psychological and Brain Sciences) mavens may chooseto to participate in the emphasis program by completing extra coursework, presenting their research, and taking cognitive science-related questions as central to their studies. [2] The program's goal is to give students an appreciation of the interdisciplinary study of thinking, perception, and intelligent behavior as determined jointly by the nature of the environment and by the internal architecture of the intelligent agent, whether human, animal, or machine. [3] The Cognitive Science Program reflects the intersecting, interdisciplinary interests of affiliated faculty and students in the College of Letters & Sciences, Gevirtz Graduate School of Education, and the College of Engineering. [2] Students who meet the Cognitive Science Emphasis requirements will graduate with a Ph.D. from their home department, along with wording on their transcript stating they have earned a Graduate Emphasis in Cognitive Science. [2]
ScholarshipType: Graduate students may be supported through a combination of fellowships, grants, and teaching or research assistantships. [88]

ProgramName: Emphasis in Computational Science and Engineering
Department: Departments of Chemical Engineering, Computer Science, Earth Science, Ecology, Evolution and Marine Biology, Electrical and Computer Engineering, Mathematics, and Mechanical Engineering
Concentration: Emphasis in Computational Science and Engineering
Description: The Departments of Chemical Engineering, Computer Science, Electrical and Computer Engineering, Mathematics, and Mechanical and Environmental Engineering, and Geology offer an interdisciplinary Master's and Ph.D. degree emphasis in Computational Science and Engineering (CSE). [1] Although CSE includes elements from computer science, applied mathematics, engineering and science, it focuses on the integration of knowledge and methodologies from all of these disciplines and, as such, is a subject distinct from any of them. [1] All students pursuing an emphasis in CSE must complete the following course requirements: Numerical Methods: Math 206A-B-C-D. (Students must complete at least three.) Parallel Computing: Computer Science 240A-B. (Students must take at least one. Computer Science 140A-B is an acceptable alternative.) Applied Mathematics: Students must take a two course sequence from either the Mathematics 243A-B or the Mathematics 246A-B sequence. [1]

ProgramName: Emphasis in Demography
Description: The departments of Anthropology, Economics, Geography, Sociology and Global Studies are now offering, in cooperation with the Broom Center, a PhD Emphasis in Demography. The goal of this program is to give doctoral students in the five departments an opportunity to gain a broader interdisciplinary understanding of concepts and methods in population-related research, beyond the resources available in their home departments. [9] Requirements include completion of a core course on human population dynamics including fertility, mortality, and migration, regular attendance at the biweekly Broom seminar, completion of three population-related courses including one outside your own discipline, and dissertation research with a focus in demography. [9] Upon completion of the requirements, the student will receive a Demography Emphasis certificate when their disciplinary PhD is awarded. [9]
ScholarshipType: fellowships/ traineeships, teaching assistantships (TA's), research assistantships (RA's), Federal Work-Study, and loans. [67]

ProgramName: Emphasis in Environment and Society
Description: The Interdepartmental Ph.D. Emphasis in Environment and Society (IEES) provides UCSB doctoral students in participating departments an opportunity to receive training and mentorship in interdisciplinary environmental studies and sciences beyond the normal scope of their degree programs. The goal is to equip student participants with the interdisciplinary tools—including methods, concepts, and analytical frameworks—necessary to communicate across disciplines and tackle complex environmental issues. Students who complete the requirements will receive a certificate, and a note will be added to their transcript indicating they have earned an Emphasis in Environment and Society. The program is designed to create an interdisciplinary community of students and faculty, enhance mentorship opportunities, and improve competitiveness in the academic job market.

ProgramName: Emphasis in European Medieval Studies
Concentration: Optional Ph.D. Emphasis in European Medieval Studies
Description: The Medieval Studies Program offers an interdisciplinary doctoral emphasis to students previously admitted to a Ph.D. program in the Departments of Theater and Dance, English, French and Italian, History, History of Art and Architecture, Music, Religious Studies, and Spanish and Portuguese. [3] The interdisciplinary Ph.D. emphasis in Medieval Studies is designed primarily for Ph.D. candidates specializing in European and Mediterranean cultures (roughly 500-1500), although students focusing on other medieval cultures may also participate if they fulfill the requirements. [4] The faculty in the Medieval Studies Program believe that the emphasis will enhance students' prospects for academic positions by affirming that they have analyzed medieval society from a multidisciplinary perspective, approached its society and culture through original sources in more than one language, and received formal training in technical skills necessary for research with archival or manuscript materials. [4]

[91]

ProgramName: Emphasis in Information Technology and Society
Concentration: ['Area 1 – Culture and History', 'Area 2 – Society and Behavior']
Description: The Emphasis in Information Technology and Society brings together doctoral students in engineering, science, social science, and the humanities to engage in multidisciplinary coursework and research into the cultural and societal changes resulting from the use of information technologies. [1] It is a degree supplement that provides multi-disciplinary training for graduate students in participating departments planning dissertations dealing with the societal implications of information technology. [3] The Emphasis features a structured set of courses that may be taught individually or collaboratively by faculty across disciplines in the participating departments. [1] To be eligible for admission to the Emphasis, students must be enrolled and in good standing in their home department. [1]

Emphasis in Translation Studies
Description: Comparative Literature at UC Santa Barbara is home to the Graduate Emphasis in Translation Studies and the Translation Studies Minor. [16] Courses in Translation Studies engage the theoretical questions that are germane to a philosophy of translation and that inform the practice of translation. [9] To participate, you must be an enrolled graduate student in good academic standing pursuing a PhD in Classics, Comparative Literature, East Asian Studies, English, French, German, Religious Studies or Spanish, with an interest in literary translation and competency in more than one language. [9] The emphasis requires the completion of 16 units, including Comparative Literature 260: Literary Translation: Theory and Practice, or an equivalent course. [9] Colleagues affiliated with Translation Studies are often literary translators, with some broadening the scope of linguistic, literary, and cultural translations, while others explore intersections between the Humanities and the Sciences. [16]

ProgramName: Emphasis in Writing Studies
Certificate in College and University Teaching
Description: The Certificate in College and University Teaching (CCUT) is designed for doctoral students who wish to demonstrate superior competence and experience in preparation for teaching at the university or college level. [18] Official CCUT certificates are issued by the Office of the Registrar and are noted on the student's transcript. [18] The Certificate is awarded in conjunction with a Ph.D. or MFA degree upon completion. [18] The awarding of the Certificate signifies that the applicant has demonstrated competencies in applying research and theory to teaching, planning and conducting classes with equitable and inclusive strategies, evaluating instructional designs, effectively instructing a class as the Instructor of Record, and discussing their teaching philosophy and practices. [18]

ProgramName: Graduate Program in Management Practice
Description: For highly motivated graduate students seeking a structured and diploma-enhancing business education, Technology Management offers a UC-recognized graduate certificate. [1, 5] The Graduate Program in Management Practice (GPMP) is open to UC Santa Barbara master's degree students and Ph.D. candidates from any major. [1, 5] Like the Undergraduate Certificate program, GPMP introduces students across academic disciplines to the fundamentals of business, finance, management, marketing, and strategy. [1, 5] However, GPMP coursework also takes a deeper dive into Business Strategy & Leadership, Innovation & Management, New Venture Marketing & Finance, and offers an option to specialize in start-up or established businesses. [1] Students are expected to complete 18 units in GPMP. [1, 5] The progression of classes emphasizes first the business foundation needed in a business or entrepreneurial environment. [1, 5] After completing foundational coursework, students will select one of two emphases, entrepreneurial or corporate, focusing on the context of career expectations beyond their studies. [5] Finally, the GPMP certificate requires a meaningful experience putting these ideas into practice, whereby students will choose one of the following: an Internship or participation in the New Venture Competition. [1, 5]

ProgramName: Graduate Certificate in Bilingual School Psychology
Description: Candidates with bilingual proficiency (oral language, reading, and writing) can complete a specialization in bilingual-culturally responsive school psychology through the Graduate Certificate in Bilingual School Psychology (BSP). [8] Students who elect to complete the Bilingual Specialization receive training that enables them to provide school psychological services to children in both monolingual and bilingual settings. [8] Additional coursework focuses more intensively on the theory and practice of bilingual / multicultural education and methods of providing psychological services in the target language. [8] The Graduate Certificate in Bilingual School Psychology requires students to complete all requirements for the PPS credential program, and one additional course (4 credits) emphasizing bilingual and multicultural education. [8] Candidates are also required to attend quarterly Bilingual Roundtable meetings and complete their practicum and internship at bilingual / culturally diverse sites and receive supervision from bilingual school psychologists. [8] Candidates who are pursuing the Graduate Certificate in Bilingual School Psychology will need to demonstrate discipline specific language proficiency in both English and a second language as well as proficiency in culturally responsive school psychology practice. [8] The mission of the Graduate Certificate in Bilingual School Psychology program is to support and promote the professional preparation of bilingual school psychologists to meet the needs of multilingual children and their families. [8, 10]

ProgramName: Bachelor of Science in Actuarial Science
Requirements: To be admitted to the full major, students must complete all pre-major courses with a 2.5 or higher UC grade-point average. All pre-major courses must be completed with a grade of “C” or better. Students are permitted to repeat a maximum of two pre-major courses. Only one repeat is allowed in each course. While completing required preparation, students are classified as a Pre-Actuarial Science major. Entry into the pre-major does not guarantee admission to full major status. [47, 50]

ProgramName: Bachelor of Arts in Anthropology
Fees: $15,647.76/Year for California residents (2024-2025); $48,641.76/Year for non-residents (2024-2025). This does not include other fees or living expenses.
Description: The aim of the anthropology major is threefold: (1) to prepare for graduate school those students who wish to work professionally in anthropology; (2) to prepare students for careers in secondary education or in social work; and (3) to provide a background in behavioral studies for students who desire a broad education in either the biological or the social sciences. Students interested in modern social and cultural groups choose an emphasis in cultural anthropology. Students interested in understanding the biological underpinnings and ecological/evolutionary adaptations of modern and ancient humans choose and emphasis in biological anthropology. Students interested in ancient peoples from both cultural and biological perspectives choose an emphasis in archaeology. Students who prefer a broad overview of all of these topics should choose the general major without an emphasis.
MinGPA: 3.0 for California residents in A-G courses; 3.4 for non-residents in A-G courses for admission. A 2.0 cumulative GPA is required for graduation.

Bachelor of Arts in Anthropology—Cultural Emphasis
Description: Cultural anthropology addresses broad questions about what it means to be human in contemporary societies and cultures, as well as those of the recent past. Cultural anthropologists systematically explore topics such as technology and material culture, social organization, economies, political and legal systems, language, ideologies and religions, health and illness, and social change.

Importantly, you'll also develop an interdisciplinary knowledge of various fields relating to Asia: literature, film, art, history, anthropology, religious studies, politics, and economics. Finally, you'll acquire a comparative context for your understanding of Asia in its relations with the US and other parts of the world. [51, 53]

Bachelor of Music in Music—Voice Emphasis
Description: The Bachelor of Music degree is a professional degree, open by entrance audition. [59] The majority of courses are in performance, theory, musicianship, and history with intense study in applied music, requiring a high level of proficiency in an instrument, voice, or composition upon entrance. [59] Applicants seeking admission to the Bachelor of Music are required to pass an entrance audition. [59] The core academic courses: music theory, musicianship, and music history, is similar to the BA Music Studies, Western Art Music major. [59] BM students are also required to pass end-of-year first-year and sophomore auditions (performance exams for a faculty jury), and public Junior and Senior Recitals to continue in the degree. [59] The Department of Music offers a variety of undergraduate and graduate programs for Music students. [68] Undergraduates may pursue either a Bachelor of Arts (BA), or a Bachelor of Music (BM) with a number of possible performance emphases. [68] These include a BM with optional emphases in Piano, Voice, Strings (Violin, Viola, Cello, Double Bass), Woodwinds (Flute, Clarinet, Oboe, Bassoon), Brass (Horn, Trumpet, Trombone, Tuba), Percussion, and Composition. [68]

ProgramName: Bachelor of Arts in Music Studies
Description: The Bachelor of Arts in Music Studies (B.A.) balances musical studies in history, musicianship, theory, and performance. [2] There are multiple tracks within the B.A. program that emphasize different areas and approaches to music. As a student in the program, you can choose from a range of courses, including hip-hop, musical systems from around the globe, electronic music, and film music. [2] You'll also have opportunities for performance through individual instruction and ensemble participation. Additionally, you can gain hands-on experience through music cognition research, ecomusicology research, and independent study opportunities. [2]

ProgramName: Bachelor of Arts in Music Studies—Ethnomusicology Emphasis
Description: For specific degree requirements, see the BA, Music Studies with an emphasis in Ethnomusicology in the Music Department, Undergraduate Program section of UC Santa Barbara's General Catalog. [26] The Ethnomusicology Program at UC Santa Barbara consists of core courses in three areas: Regional Studies, including the Middle East, South Asia, Eastern Europe, American folk and vernacular music, Japan, Indonesia, and Mexico; Issues - such as anthropology of music, globalization, cosmopolitanism, tourism, sound studies, and gender studies; and Methods - such as theories and methods in ethnomusicology, fieldwork, tuning and temperament, and maqam. [26] The program has the following performance ensembles: Middle East Ensemble, Music of India Ensemble, Indonesian Gamelan Ensemble, Gospel Choir, and periodically, a Polish Ensemble, an Appalachian Ensemble, and an Afro-Brazilian Ensemble. [26]

ProgramName: Bachelor of Arts in Music Studies—Interdisciplinary Studies of Music Emphasis
Description: The B.A. in Music Studies with an emphasis in Interdisciplinary Studies is intended for students with a broad interest in music as a cultural, historical, and social phenomenon. This emphasis is designed for students who may be interested in a career in music journalism, music librarianship, or arts administration, as well as for those who wish to pursue a graduate degree in musicology, ethnomusicology, or music theory. The curriculum for this emphasis provides students with a broad-based education in the various fields of music studies, including musicology, ethnomusicology, and music theory, as well as performance.

ProgramName: Bachelor of Arts in Philosophy—Core Philosophy
Description: As a student in Philosophy, you'll grapple with funda- mental questions that engage all reflective people, but which apparently cannot be answered by the empirical sciences: Are our actions determined by forces over which we lack control, or is free choice possible? What distinguishes people from (non-human) animals? Are there objective standards of right and wrong, or is morality subjective? Does altruism exist or are people essentially self-interested? What are the limits of human knowledge? Can machines think? What is the relationship between mind and body? [10]

ProgramName: Bachelor of Arts in Philosophy—Ethics & Public Policy
Bachelor of Arts in Physics
Bachelor of Science in Physics
Description: Physics is the most fundamental of the sciences. It is the basis for our understanding of the world around us, from the smallest constituents of matter to the universe as a whole. UCSB is a world-renowned institution for physics. The physics major is a flexible program that offers a rich and diverse learning environment. Students are exposed to a broad curriculum that covers the main areas of physics, including mechanics, electricity and magnetism, quantum mechanics, and statistical mechanics. They also have the opportunity to take advanced electives in specialized topics such as astrophysics, condensed matter physics, and particle physics. The program is designed to provide students with a strong foundation in the principles of physics and to prepare them for a variety of careers in research, education, and industry.

ProgramName: Bachelor of Arts in Religious Studies
Fees: The estimated tuition for the 2025-2026 academic year is $15,444 for California residents and $47,332 for out-of-state students. [76]
Description: The bachelor of arts in religious studies, by exploring a variety of questions and methods, prepares students for a wide range of professions. The academic study of religion is interdisciplinary, involving the study of texts, histories, cultures, and theories. Courses address such topics as the religions of ancient India; the history of modern Islam; religions of East Asia; the history of Christianity; Judaism and Jewish identity; religions of America; religion and politics; religion, the media, and popular culture; the social psychology of religion; and the nature of religious experience. The department’s courses cover a wide range of religious traditions, including Buddhism, Christianity, Confucianism, Hinduism, Islam, Judaism, and Daoism. In addition, many courses are cross-cultural and comparative, and they explore the theoretical and methodological issues involved in the study of religion.
ScholarshipAmount: The Regents Scholarship offers an award of $5,000 per year. [77]
ScholarshipType: UCSB offers various scholarships, including the prestigious merit-based Regents Scholarship. [77] Need-based and other types of scholarships are also available through the Office of Financial Aid and Scholarships. [53, 54]

ProgramName: Bachelor of Arts in Renaissance Studies
ScholarshipType: Need-based and merit-based scholarships are available. [20, 38]

ProgramName: Bachelor of Arts in Russian & East European Studies
Description: Situated on the threshold between Europe and Asia, Islam and Christianity, and East and West, Russia has always had a culture and identity dependent on its changing relationship with other cultures and nations, including those in Eastern and Central Europe. [5] With vast natural resources and global significance, Russia is a country whose language, politics, and culture we can't afford not to understand better. [5] Russia's world-renowned art, literature, film, and music can help you understand this vast and diverse country beyond the headlines. [5] As a student in the program, you'll take courses covering different aspects of Russian and East European culture taught by dedicated and expert faculty who will give you all the personal attention you need to succeed. [5] Of course, the best way to understand another culture is through its language! We offer world-class instruction in the Russian language at all levels of proficiency. [5] Career options for majors and minors include business, government, law, medicine, travel, education, and translation. [5]

ProgramName: Bachelor of Arts in Spanish
Bachelor of Arts in Statistics and Data Science
Description: The Statistics and Data Science major at UC Santa Barbara combines statistical theory with practical data analysis skills. Students learn to tackle real-world problems using statistical modeling, data visualization, machine learning, and programming. The program prepares graduates for careers in data science, analytics, and research, offering hands-on experience and strong industry connections in a collaborative, innovative environment. [3] The B.A. in Statistics and Data Science is a basic degree intended for students interested in general training and statistics and the use of statistical methods in the social sciences, psychology, business and management, biological and environmental sciences, etc. [3]
MinGPA: 3.0 for California residents, 3.4 for non-residents (for the general UC system)

ProgramName: Bachelor of Science in Statistics and Data Science
Description: The Bachelor of Science in Statistics and Data Science equips students to execute all stages of data analysis, apply common techniques in statistics and machine learning, respect the principles and best practices of reproducible data science and articulate the role of statistics and data science in a just and ethical society. [1] The program provides a strong foundation in the established field of statistics while reaching into the modern and emerging field of data science. [1] Graduates of this program may be hired as statisticians or data scientists who are able to collect and curate large volumes of data, bring statistical and machine learning methods to bear on new questions and create data pipelines and workflows that transform digital information into actionable insights. [1] Students will also be prepared to succeed in graduate studies. [1]

To join the B.F.A. program, you'll be required to audition either at the end of the freshman year or the beginning of the sophomore year for acceptance. The program combines rigorous classical training with individual expression and creativity and is geared toward preparation for entry into the professional theater industry and/or Master of Fine Arts/conservatory programs. Description: The CCS Mathematics Major provides a rigorous education in mathematics to highly motivated, self-directed an environment in which students can develop high-level abilities in mathematics and become well prepared for careers in academia or industry. [1] The program provides students with a flexible plan of study, giving them the opportunity to tailor an individualized program according to their interests. [1] Students are encouraged to take advantage of the many summer research opportunities and internships available in the Mathematics Department and other institutions. [1] Students take their core first year courses as well as some second year courses in CCS, and then complete all upper-division courses within the Mathematics Department. [1] The CCS sequences give students a thorough introduction to basic mathematics with an emphasis on problem solving, communication, and collaboration. [1] In consultation with their faculty advisor, students may have the opportunity to take graduate-level courses as early as appropriate. [1] The skills and abilities learned in CCS courses enable students to pursue original mathematical activities, often making significant contributions during their undergraduate careers. [1] This work culminates in a senior capstone project, prepared prior to graduation. [1]

ProgramName: Bachelor of Arts in Physics (Creative Studies)
Description: The physics program in the College of Creative Studies provides a rigorous physics education at one of the premiere research universities in the country. Our small class sizes and close student-faculty interaction create an intimate environment where students can think deeply and critically about physics. At the same time, students are encouraged to take advantage of the many research opportunities that are available at UCSB. Students develop a wide and deep understanding of physics and are well-prepared for graduate work in physics or related fields. As in other fields of study in CCS, students enjoy unparalleled academic freedom in working with faculty advisors to design their course of study. CCS Physics is a joint program between the College of Creative Studies and the UCSB Physics Department. Students take their core first- and second-year courses in CCS, and complete upper-division courses within CCS and the Physics Department. The two-year CCS sequence gives students a thorough introduction to basic physics with an emphasis on problem solving, communication, and collaboration. As part of the course, students attend problem sessions in which they present their work to each other. Second-year students will also take a three-quarter laboratory course designed to prepare them for participation in modern physics research. Here students develop the mindset and many of the skills required of an experimentalist. [2]

[9] The program strives to provide a holistic learning experience in both culture and language. [9]

The Core Plan involves taking one lower-division English course (4 units) and 20 upper-division units distributed as follows: 4.0 units in literature before 1700, 4.0 units in literature from 1700-1900, and 12.0 units of English electives. Description: Game Studies is an interdisciplinary minor for students interested in game studies of all types who wish to acquire focused training in the visual and material culture, history, theory, development, programming, narrative, and production of games. [15, 20] This minor encompasses the investigation of games from a range of different perspectives, including the aesthetics of games, the cultural and historical context surrounding games, the social, political and economic implications of games, and the design (visual and narrative) of games. [20] The program involves scholars and courses from various departments including History of Art & Architecture, Film and Media Studies, English, Writing, Computer Science, Communication, and Psychology and Brain Sciences. [15, 20] The minor aims to provide students with concrete, marketable skills in script writing, programming, modeling, and teamwork. [20]

Description: The Minor in Poverty, Inequality and Social Justice provides students with the tools to understand the structural and political roots, dynamics and consequences of poverty and inter-sectional inequality; conduct original research; and engage meaningfully in efforts to address poverty through policy, practice and social action. [5] The core components of this Minor involve a gateway course on poverty, inequality and social justice in historical and global context, three upper-division electives chosen from an interdisciplinary range of fields, an internship, and a capstone course. [3] The Minor is offered through the Department of History and is interdisciplinary in scope. [5] It is affiliated with the UCSB Blum Center on Poverty, Inequality, and Democracy. [5]

ProgramName: Minor in Professional Writing
Concentration: ['Professional Editing', 'Multimedia Communication', 'Business Communication', 'Writing and Civic Engagement', 'Science Communication', 'Journalism']
Description: The Professional Writing Minor is an opportunity for undergraduates to expand their communication skills through two capstone courses and a writing internship during their senior year. [22] Students considering the minor should think of it as an apprenticeship in the world of professional writing, not simply as a set of courses in which someone will tell you what to do. [22] The Professional Writing Minor is separated into distinct tracks: Professional Editing, Multimedia Communication, Business Communication, Writing and Civic Engagement, Science Communication, and Journalism. [22] Each track includes two capstone courses and an internship. [22] Professional Writing Minors must be more than good students. [22] They must be excellent writers and editors. [22] They must be able and willing to function in a professional internship environment, to accept responsibility, to demonstrate initiative, to complete assignments, to meet deadlines, and to work collegially in group projects. [22]

ProgramName: Minor in Russian and East European Studies
Description: The Russian minor requires 15 hours of coursework (5 courses). It is designed to allow students to achieve a significant level of proficiency in Russian and insight into Russian culture as a secondary area of concentration in addition to their major.

ProgramName: Minor in Science and Mathematics Education
Description: The Minor in Science and Mathematics Education is for science, mathematics, and engineering undergraduates interested in learning and teaching others about mathematics and science. [3] There are two tracks in this minor: one for undergraduates interested in becoming elementary school teachers and one for undergraduates interested in becoming secondary science and mathematics teachers. [2, 3] The program is part of CalTeach, a UC system-wide initiative designed to recruit and mentor undergraduates for careers as K-12 teachers in science and mathematics, involving a sequence of courses and practical classroom experience. [2, 6]

ProgramName: Minor in Sociology
Description: Sociology is the systematic study of social life. Through empirical inquiry, sociologists seek to understand the process by which societies, communities, institutions, and organizations are created, maintained, undermined, and transformed, and the ways in which social life shapes individuals. [22] The Department of Sociology at UCSB is known for its diversity of perspective and for its support for emerging areas of study and innovative approaches to theory, method, and empirical inquiry. [22, 23] In addition to providing the core of a liberal arts education, the sociology minor can also serve as preparation for a career in such fields as law, management, urban and environmental planning, corrections, journalism, teaching, social work, and other service professions. [22, 23]

ProgramName: Minor in Spanish
Description: The Department of Spanish and Portuguese offers a Major in Spanish (Bachelor of Arts) and a Minor in Spanish, open to students from any major across campus. [2] At the introductory level, students build fluency in speaking and writing through a carefully designed sequence of language courses. [2] At the advanced level, students take courses in the history of the language, linguistics, and the literatures and cultures of Spain and Latin America. [2] Majors can choose to focus on language, literature, culture, or a combination of these areas. [2] Many students pair their Spanish major with a second major in fields like the humanities, social sciences, or natural sciences, enhancing their academic and career opportunities. [2] This combination broadens their perspective, develops valuable skills, and prepares them for a wide range of professions in a globalized world. [2]

ProgramName: Minor in Speech and Hearing Sciences
Description: The Speech-Language Sciences and Disorders minor provides students with much of the preparation for pursuing professional degrees to become speech-language pathologists and audiologists. Courses comprising the minor cover areas that are foundational for graduate study in Communication Sciences and Disorders, including acoustic phonetics, articulatory phonetics, auditory phonetics, language acquisition, psychology of language, and clinical linguistics. [27]

Minor in Translation Studies
Description: The Undergraduate Minor in Translation Studies introduces students to the histories, theories, and practices of translation, through a core course on literary translation taught in the Comparative Literature Program and a variety of translation-related courses selected from different departments in the Humanities and Social Sciences. [16] The Minor in Translation Studies is intended for all students who would like to build on UCSB's language training by developing their mastery of the art of translation. [16] Translating between languages helps students to enrich and develop their linguistic abilities and to grow as writers and readers. [16] But translation is also a way of thinking. [16] The Minor trains students to think transculturally, that is, to better understand the interactions between cultures, media, discourses, and disciplines and to move more easily between them. [16]
